sub_graphs.title: EIP-5: Memory Protection and Sub-call Data Isolation
sub_graphs.description: Models the security boundaries around memory access during CALL operations

nodes.label: Output Area Reserved
nodes.description: Calling contract has designated a specific memory region for output

nodes.label: Enforce Output Bounds
nodes.description: Limit data writing to designated output area [output_start, output_start + output_size)

nodes.label: Output Data Bounded
nodes.description: Return data is constrained to the specified output region

nodes.label: Arbitrary Memory Write Prevented
nodes.description: Sub-call cannot write to arbitrary memory locations outside designated area

external_entities.name: Calling Contract
external_entities.description: Contract that specifies output memory area for security

external_entities.name: Called Contract
external_entities.description: Sub-routine that returns data constrained to output bounds

ambiguities.text: The proposal states gas is charged 'only for memory that is actually written to' but the formula charges for output_start + min(output_size, n), which may include unwritten bytes if output_start > current MSIZE.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume gas is charged for the memory expansion required to reach output_start + min(output_size, n), regardless of what portion contains actual data. This is standard EVM memory expansion semantics.

ambiguities.text: The behavior when output_start + output_size overflows 2^256-1 is not explicitly specified.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume overflow handling follows standard EVM arithmetic (modulo 2^256) and that implementations must handle the edge case of output_size = 2^256-1 for dynamic sizing detection.

implicit_assumptions.description: The calling contract trusts that the output bounds enforcement prevents the called contract from corrupting memory outside the designated output area.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Called contracts could overwrite arbitrary memory in the calling contract, leading to state corruption or control flow hijacking.

implicit_assumptions.description: Contracts using output_size = 2^256-1 for dynamic sizing must be prepared to handle the gas cost of any return data size.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts could run out of gas unexpectedly when receiving large return data, causing transaction failures.

implicit_assumptions.description: Objects stored in memory after CALL operations must be relocatable since absolute positions may change based on actual return data size.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts with hardcoded memory offsets may experience data corruption when memory layout changes dynamically.
